title: Minimum Number of K Consecutive Bit Flips
summary: Given a binary array nums and an integer k, find the minimum number of k-bit flips required to make all elements in the array equal to 1.
statement: Given a binary array nums and an integer k, find the minimum number of k-bit flips required to make all elements in the array equal to 1. A k-bit flip involves selecting a contiguous subarray of length k and flipping all 0s to 1s and all 1s to 0s within that subarray. If it is impossible to achieve this, return -1.
constraints: A move flips exactly k consecutive bits.
Return the minimum moves to make every bit one, or -1 if impossible.
hints: At position i, no later window can change it, so an effective zero forces a flip starting there.
Track active flip parity and when each flip began.
Expire i-k, compare bit with parity, and start a flip or fail if fewer than k cells remain.
Every greedy flip is forced, making the result minimal and unique when feasible.

tests.explanation: Flip each zero individually, requiring two moves.
The final zero cannot be flipped without changing a preceding one, so return -1.
